brief.text:
The access desk reads one badge at a time and tells you which doors it opens. Reads it straight off what you punch in - and it never checks whether you punched in one instruction or two.

So give it two. Let it read your badge like always. Then, in the same breath, slip it a second order it was never meant to take: flip the vault door to OPEN. Close with a quick look at the result so you know the order landed.

One punch. Two moves.
brief.objective: Stack a second command onto the badge read and force the vault door open.

debrief.explanation: Two failures again: your badge is concatenated into the SQL, and the desk runs the whole string as a batch - so a semicolon ends the app's read and starts a statement of your own. After 'B-1001' you close the quote, add ; UPDATE door_acl SET granted = 1 WHERE door = 'VAULT' (the real damage), then a second SELECT to verify, and -- to swallow the leftover quote. SQLite executes all of it in order: the harmless read, your write, and the confirming read. The extra result set is the proof the stacked statement ran.

vulnerableCodeVariants.label: Node.js (pg / mysql2)
Python (sqlite3 / psycopg2)
vulnerableCodeVariants.code:
# VULNERABLE - executescript() runs the WHOLE string as a batch of statements
sql = f"SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE badge = '{badge}'"
cur.executescript(sql)
# The stacked "; UPDATE door_acl SET granted=1 WHERE door='VAULT'" rides in as its own statement.
# psycopg2: one execute() with ';'-separated text runs the batch too.

vulnerableCodeVariants.label: PHP (PDO)
Java (JDBC)
C# / .NET (ADO.NET)
Go (database/sql)
Ruby on Rails (ActiveRecord)
vulnerableCodeVariants.code:
# VULNERABLE - connection.execute runs the raw string, batch and all
sql = "SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE badge = '#{badge}'"
ActiveRecord::Base.connection.execute(sql)
# The stacked "; UPDATE door_acl SET granted=1 WHERE door='VAULT'" rides in as its own statement.

vulnerableCodeVariants.label: Laravel (Query Builder)
Django (ORM)
vulnerableCodeVariants.code:
# VULNERABLE - executescript() (sqlite backend) runs the whole string as a batch
from django.db import connection
sql = f"SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE badge = '{badge}'"
connection.cursor().executescript(sql)
# The stacked "; UPDATE door_acl SET granted=1 WHERE door='VAULT'" rides in as its own statement.

vulnerableCodeVariants.label: Spring Boot (JdbcTemplate)

secureCodeVariants.label: Node.js (pg / mysql2)
Python (sqlite3 / psycopg2)
secureCodeVariants.code:
# SECURE - execute() runs a SINGLE statement and binds the value
cur.execute("SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE badge = ?", (badge,))
rows = cur.fetchall()
# The ';'-payload becomes an inert string; executescript() is the footgun to avoid.
# psycopg2: cur.execute("... badge = %s", (badge,)) is single-statement too.

secureCodeVariants.label: PHP (PDO)
Java (JDBC)
C# / .NET (ADO.NET)
Go (database/sql)
Ruby on Rails (ActiveRecord)
secureCodeVariants.code:
# SECURE - the placeholder binds the value; ActiveRecord runs a single query
rows = DoorAcl.where("badge = ?", badge).to_a
# The stacked ';' stays an inert string inside the badge, never a second command.
# Hash form binds too: DoorAcl.where(badge: badge)

secureCodeVariants.label: Laravel (Query Builder)
Django (ORM)
secureCodeVariants.code:
# SECURE - the ORM parameterizes every lookup and runs a single query
rows = DoorAcl.objects.filter(badge=badge)
# The ';'-payload becomes an inert string; never route input into executescript().
# .raw() still binds: DoorAcl.objects.raw("... WHERE badge = %s", [badge])

secureCodeVariants.label: Spring Boot (JdbcTemplate)

debrief.takeaway: A question should ask one thing. Bind the value AND let the driver run a single statement - so a semicolon is a syntax error, not a to-do list.

database.schemaSql: CREATE TABLE door_acl (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, badge TEXT, door TEXT, granted INTEGER);

query.template: SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE badge = '{{input:badge}}'
query.description: Badge access lookup (the whole input string is executed as a batch)

winCondition.reason: A second statement rode in behind the badge read - the vault door flipped to OPEN and the verify read proved it.

hints.text: This desk doesn't just read your badge - it runs whatever you hand it, top to bottom. A single lookup is polite. Nothing's stopping you from being impolite and handing it a second instruction.

Close the quote, end the read with a semicolon, then write your own statement: UPDATE door_acl to set granted = 1 on the VAULT door. Add one more SELECT so the change shows up as a result, and finish with -- to comment out the trailing quote.

In the badge box:  B-1001'; UPDATE door_acl SET granted = 1 WHERE door = 'VAULT'; SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE door = 'VAULT' --   The UPDATE is the break-in; the final SELECT is your receipt.

inputs.badge: B-1001'; UPDATE door_acl SET granted = 1 WHERE door = 'VAULT'; SELECT door, granted FROM door_acl WHERE door = 'VAULT' --

expectedSolution.note: Three statements run: the app's read (rows), your UPDATE (the side effect - VAULT granted flips 0 -> 1), and a verify SELECT (rows). Two row-producing statements => an extra result set surfaces => win. A plain badge like B-1001 runs one statement and changes nothing.
